next_steps.text: Wash it under running water before eating or cutting. Washing can reduce bacteria but does not eliminate them.

storage_fallback.text: Keep perishable produce such as strawberries, lettuce and herbs in a clean refrigerator at 40°F or below, and refrigerate anything pre-cut or packaged. If you are unsure whether an item should be refrigerated, ask your grocer.

checks.text: Cut away any damaged or bruised areas before eating, and throw away any produce that looks rotten.
Look for visible mold. If it is covered with mold, discard it.

next_steps.text: If it looks rotten, throw it away.
If it is covered with mold, discard it, and do not sniff it, which can cause respiratory trouble.

storage.text: Clean the spot where it was stored, and check nearby produce it touched. Mold spreads quickly in fruits and vegetables.

checks.text: Look for visible mold or areas that look rotten. FreshNet does not detect mold or any other specific cause.

storage.text: Apples can sit at room temperature, away from direct sunlight, for under a week. Refrigerate them for longer.
Store bananas at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. In the refrigerator the skin turns black and they do not gain good sweetness.
Store peppers at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. They can go in the refrigerator for 1 to 3 days if you use them soon after taking them out.
Store carrots in the refrigerator in a perforated plastic bag in the produce drawer, apart from ripe fruit, which can give carrots a bitter taste.
Store cucumbers at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. They can go in the refrigerator for 1 to 3 days if you use them soon after taking them out.

spoiled_mold_point.text: If it has mold, discard it. USDA says soft produce such as cucumbers can be contaminated below the surface. Do not sniff it.

storage.text: Store mangoes at room temperature, away from direct sunlight.
Okra keeps best in a cool place of 50 to 60°F. If you have none, refrigerate it for no longer than 5 days and use it soon after taking it out.
Store oranges at room temperature, away from direct sunlight.
Store potatoes in a well-ventilated spot in the pantry, and protect them from light to avoid greening.
Store strawberries in a clean refrigerator at 40°F or below.
Store whole tomatoes at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. In the refrigerator even red tomatoes lose flavor, and pink ones do not turn red.

spoiled_mold_point.text: If it has mold, discard it. USDA says soft produce such as tomatoes can be contaminated below the surface. Do not sniff it.
